motifs.name: Social Energy Orientation
motifs.summary: How a framework encodes social activation, outward engagement, and inward recharge.
motifs.description: A house translation axis for frameworks that speak about extraversion, introversion, social charge, or preferred outward intensity without assuming they all mean the same thing.

motifs.name: Exploratory Openness
motifs.summary: Appetite for novelty, imagination, curiosity, and experiential exploration.
motifs.description: A recurring motif across trait, style, and symbolic systems that captures interest in novelty, complexity, imagination, and expansion beyond routine.

motifs.name: Pattern Abstraction Preference
motifs.summary: Preference for pattern-level abstraction versus concrete detail.
motifs.description: A motif for systems that distinguish concrete sensing, intuitive patterning, symbolic interpretation, or abstraction-heavy sense making.

motifs.name: Structure and Closure Preference
motifs.summary: Preference for closure, planning, and constraint versus openness and flexibility.
motifs.description: A house bridge for constructs that describe orderliness, planning, decisiveness, structure seeking, or resistance to imposed closure.

motifs.name: Attachment and Closeness Regulation
motifs.summary: How a framework encodes safety, proximity, dependence, and distance in close relationships.
motifs.description: A relationship-layer motif for security, anxiety, avoidance, availability, reassurance seeking, and closeness management.

motifs.name: Relational Care Signaling
motifs.summary: Preferred channels for expressing and receiving care, validation, and recognition.
motifs.description: A motif for frameworks that describe how care becomes legible, especially in relational preference systems and practical communication grammars.

motifs.name: Affective Reactivity
motifs.summary: Sensitivity to stress, threat, volatility, and emotional perturbation.
motifs.description: A recurrent motif spanning trait, attachment, shadow, and stress-oriented systems that speak to reactivity, anxiety, emotional load, or instability.

motifs.name: Prosociality and Exploitiveness
motifs.summary: Orientation toward fairness, reciprocity, care, manipulation, or extraction.
motifs.description: A house motif for comparing prosocial, cooperative, and exploitative tendencies across trait, shadow, moral, and strengths-oriented systems.

motifs.name: Execution and Implementation Style
motifs.summary: How a framework encodes initiation, follow-through, improvisation, and practical doing.
motifs.description: A practical action-style motif for conative, workplace, and operational frameworks that describe how work is initiated, structured, and completed.

motifs.name: Symbolic Meaning Load
motifs.summary: Degree to which a framework functions as symbolic, cosmological, or mythic meaning language.
motifs.description: A motif for frameworks that do more than describe behavior and instead carry archetypal, spiritual, symbolic, or cosmological interpretive weight.

motifs.name: Identity Adhesion
motifs.summary: Likelihood that outputs become fused with stable self-story or social identity.
motifs.description: A house motif for comparing how strongly frameworks become identity languages rather than only descriptive or operational tools.

mappings.rationale: Big Five extraversion is one of the clearest direct encodings of outward social activation and engagement in the current corpus.
MBTI E/I clearly touches social-energy orientation, but it does so in preference language rather than a trait-intensity frame.
Openness to Experience is one of the strongest direct house anchors for novelty, imagination, and exploratory appetite.
Sensing versus intuition is not equivalent to general openness, but it is a strong preference-language signal for concrete detail versus pattern abstraction.
Judging versus perceiving is one of the cleaner typology-language handles for closure, planning, structure, and openness to emergent process.
Attachment anxiety directly names sensitivity to rejection, abandonment, and reassurance needs in close relationships.
Attachment avoidance directly names distance regulation, intimacy discomfort, and reluctance toward dependence.
Words of Affirmation is not a whole attachment construct, but it is a clear signal about how care and validation become legible.
Quality Time expresses relational care through presence and attention rather than through trait or motive description.
Neuroticism is one of the strongest direct trait-language anchors for stress sensitivity and negative affect reactivity.
High Honesty-Humility is best read as a strong inverse signal against entitlement, manipulation, and exploitative orientation.
Kolbe is one of the clearest execution-style and conation systems in the current registry, even when specific construct crosswalks remain sparse.
Human Design functions not only as a descriptive system but as a symbolic and cosmological language with heavy narrative meaning load.
Natal astrology is a strong house example of symbolic, mythic, and cosmological meaning language rather than only behavioral measurement.
The Enneagram frequently functions as durable self-story and community identity, not only as a descriptive typology.
MBTI functions widely as a social identity and shorthand self-description language even when used outside formal assessment contexts.
Higher DAT semantic distance can signal ideational novelty and exploratory association behavior, but DAT is a bounded performance task rather than a direct trait-openness measure.
The ability to generate semantically remote words may weakly overlap with abstraction-oriented pattern movement, but DAT does not directly encode stable abstraction preference.

analysis_modes.name: Orientation and Sync
analysis_modes.summary: Establish what A Person Index currently contains, what surfaces are available, and what changed before deeper work begins.
analysis_modes.purpose: Reduce avoidable drift by making current state explicit before substantive use.
intent_signals: make sure you are up to date
orient yourself to the repo or MCP
cautions: Do not imply that orientation is the same thing as framework use.
Keep repo status separate from person-level findings.

analysis_modes.name: Bounded Single-Subject Mixed Stack
analysis_modes.summary: Match and compare one person's mixed assessment stack while preserving indexed coverage, gaps, and layer boundaries.
analysis_modes.purpose: Support careful single-subject comparative work without overclaiming runtime inference.
intent_signals: what can A Person Index do with this stack
cautions: Keep unmatched frameworks visible.
Do not flatten symbolic systems into psychometric claims.

analysis_modes.name: Architecture and Capability Analysis
analysis_modes.summary: Inspect A Person Index itself as a layered comparative system rather than only as a source of person-level outputs.
analysis_modes.purpose: Support builders and advanced users who want to understand the latent operations, seams, and limits of the substrate.
intent_signals: what can this system actually do
look past the surface lego blocks
what are the seams or gaps
cautions: Do not drift from system analysis into unconstrained person narration.
Keep latent possibilities separate from already shipped capabilities.

analysis_modes.name: Run Planning
analysis_modes.summary: Decide what kind of pass should happen, what should stay inside A Person Index, and what downstream realization is appropriate before executing.
analysis_modes.purpose: Improve mode discipline, tool choice, and artifact fit before the host starts acting.
cautions: Distinguish planning from execution clearly.
Name what evidence is still missing before promising an output shape.

analysis_modes.name: Artifact Actualization
analysis_modes.summary: Use A Person Index as the comparative core while a host agent uses available tools to materialize a deliberate artifact or deliverable.
analysis_modes.purpose: Turn structured comparative understanding into a usable downstream object without losing provenance.
intent_signals: turn this into a memo or card
generate a graph or handoff file
cautions: External tools may render or package the output, but they should not redefine comparative meaning.
Keep evidence partitions visible in the final artifact.

analysis_modes.name: Contextual and Multi-Subject Comparison
analysis_modes.summary: Compare one person across contexts or time, or compare multiple people side by side, using the same comparative grammar without collapsing the scopes.
analysis_modes.purpose: Extend the substrate beyond one mixed stack while keeping semantic discipline.
intent_signals: compare work self and relational self
cautions: Comparison intensifies the risk of smoothing over missingness.
Avoid turning pairwise work into a single compatibility score.

analysis_modes.name: Trace Review
analysis_modes.summary: Review another agent's A Person Index run to see what layers were touched, where it drifted, and what support surfaces were missing.
analysis_modes.purpose: Use run traces as internal learning material without promoting them directly into canonical truth.
intent_signals: analyze how the agent used A Person Index
cautions: This is primarily an internal or advanced mode.
Do not confuse run-quality review with person-level comparative truth.

artifact_classes.name: Comparative Memo
artifact_classes.summary: A narrative artifact that explains convergence, tension, missingness, and limits across a bounded comparative pass.
artifact_classes.notes: Good default artifact when the goal is clarity without heavy visualization.

artifact_classes.name: Human Model Card
artifact_classes.summary: A structured person-model artifact that preserves provenance, paradoxes, deployment conditions, and caveats in a formal frame.
artifact_classes.notes: Should make provenance and uncertainty more visible than a plain memo.

artifact_classes.name: Agent Markdown Handoff
artifact_classes.summary: A machine-friendly markdown artifact such as agent.md, soul.md, or another downstream handoff file shaped for future agents or systems.
artifact_classes.notes: Useful when the output is meant to be consumed by another agent later.

artifact_classes.name: Context Matrix
artifact_classes.summary: A tabular or matrix artifact comparing the same subject across contexts, roles, or time slices.
artifact_classes.notes: Best when the same axes must be shown across more than one context slice.

artifact_classes.name: Pairwise Relational Sheet
artifact_classes.summary: A side-by-side artifact for two people or two stacks that emphasizes convergence, friction, and orthogonality without collapsing to one score.
artifact_classes.notes: Should foreground what is orthogonal or missing, not just what feels resonant.

artifact_classes.name: Structured Result Bundle
artifact_classes.summary: A machine-readable output that packages structured comparative findings for downstream systems or safe research return.
artifact_classes.notes: Useful when another agent or system needs a normalized handoff.

actualization_protocols.name: Single-Subject Comparative Memo
actualization_protocols.summary: Turn a bounded single-subject mixed-stack pass into a clear comparative memo while preserving matched coverage, motifs, tensions, and caveats.
steps: Match frameworks and call out unindexed items before synthesis.
Choose the right reviewed program or pack before improvising.
Separate canonical framework content, house synthesis, and downstream judgment.
Render the memo in the expression mode appropriate to the audience.
cautions: Do not hide missing coverage for the sake of narrative smoothness.
Keep symbolic, mixed, and psychometric signals distinct when explaining the result.

actualization_protocols.name: Human Model Card Realization
actualization_protocols.summary: Use the Human Model Card program frame plus host rendering tools to produce a structured downstream artifact without confusing the artifact with canonical truth.
steps: Use the Human Model Card frame to organize provenance, paradoxes, and deployment conditions.
Preserve the evidence partitions explicitly in the rendered artifact.
Use host rendering tools only after the comparative frame is stable.
cautions: A rendered card is still downstream interpretation, not ontology.
Avoid overstating mechanism or completeness.

actualization_protocols.name: Context Matrix Render
actualization_protocols.summary: Compare one subject across time or contexts and materialize the result as a matrix or table.
steps: Declare the context slices explicitly before comparison begins.
Keep the same comparative axes visible across all slices.
Mark missing or incomparable regions instead of smoothing them over.
cautions: Contextual deltas are not automatically personality change.
Sparse input should reduce confidence and output density.

actualization_protocols.name: Pairwise Relational Sheet
actualization_protocols.summary: Compare two stacks side by side and produce a relational sheet that emphasizes convergence, friction, orthogonality, and missingness.
steps: Keep each subject's stack legible before making pairwise claims.
Compare convergence, tension, and orthogonality without collapsing them into a single score.
Use visual or tabular structure when the host can support it.
cautions: Do not force reciprocal claims where the frameworks touch different layers.
Treat missing comparison seams as informative, not embarrassing.

interaction_hypotheses.summary: Attachment anxiety can make verbal reassurance feel unusually central and high-salience.
interaction_hypotheses.rationale: This pairing often amplifies the felt importance of affirmation because anxiety around availability and security can heighten the value of explicit verbal reassurance.
conditions: especially salient under uncertainty or relational ambiguity

interaction_hypotheses.summary: Desire for touch and avoidance around dependence can produce mixed relational signals.
interaction_hypotheses.rationale: Physical touch preference does not erase avoidance, but the combination can create push-pull dynamics where closeness is sought and defended against at the same time.
conditions: especially visible in close relationships under stress

interaction_hypotheses.summary: Social energy orientation and attachment regulation often get conflated but do not describe the same layer.
interaction_hypotheses.rationale: Extraversion or introversion-like patterns say little by themselves about anxiety, avoidance, or security in close attachment relationships.

interaction_hypotheses.summary: High emotional reactivity can intensify the lived impact of attachment insecurity.
interaction_hypotheses.rationale: Reactivity does not equal attachment insecurity, but the two can amplify each other in situations involving uncertainty, threat, or perceived abandonment.
conditions: especially visible during conflict or relational threat

interaction_hypotheses.summary: Symbolic meaning-heavy systems often become especially adhesive identity languages.
interaction_hypotheses.rationale: When a framework carries cosmological, archetypal, or destiny-coded meaning, users are more likely to adopt it as a durable self-story rather than as a lightweight descriptive layer.

interaction_hypotheses.summary: Strong execution-style patterns often become more legible when paired with structure and closure preferences.
interaction_hypotheses.rationale: Action style and closure preference are not identical, but together they frequently explain whether someone initiates, organizes, and completes work in stable or improvisational ways.

interaction_hypotheses.summary: Abstraction preference and closure preference can align or diverge depending on the framework and context.
interaction_hypotheses.rationale: Pattern-level thinking may coexist with either structured convergence or open-ended exploration, so this pairing should be interpreted as a tension map rather than a stable equivalence.

techniques.name: Cross-Framework Translation
techniques.purpose: Translate constructs across systems without forcing false equivalence.
techniques.summary: Compare constructs through shared motifs, relationship semantics, and epistemic bracketing rather than by naive one-to-one conversion.
steps: Identify source and target layers of personhood.
Compare through shared motifs before direct translation.
Mark overlap as strong, partial, inverse, symbolic, or incommensurable.
cautions: Do not flatten symbolic and psychometric systems into one evidence bucket.
Preserve asymmetry when one framework is broader or socially different than the other.

techniques.name: Paradox Scan
techniques.purpose: Surface load-bearing contradictions rather than averaging them away.
techniques.summary: Detect tensions across frameworks, constructs, and observations that may indicate adaptation, context splits, or multi-layer organization.
steps: List apparently conflicting signals.
Check whether the signals operate on different layers.
Preserve contradiction when it remains explanatorily useful.
cautions: Contradiction is not automatically error.
Do not turn every mismatch into pathology.

techniques.name: Contradiction Preservation
techniques.purpose: Keep the system from over-compressing a person or a framework into false coherence.
techniques.summary: Treat unresolved conflict, multiplicity, and context-dependence as data instead of noise to be smoothed out.
steps: Track incompatible but supported readings.
Label scope, context, and confidence.
Delay forced synthesis until one reading clearly dominates.
cautions: Avoid rhetorical neatness when the material is genuinely split.

techniques.name: Stable vs Adaptive Split
techniques.purpose: Separate baseline pattern from adaptation, coping, or context-driven behavior.
techniques.summary: Distinguish persistent structure from role performance, learned compensation, stress modes, or situational masking.
steps: Identify recurring signals across time.
Flag signals that only appear under specific conditions.
Keep baseline and adaptive explanations side by side.
cautions: Do not claim essence when the evidence is situational.

techniques.name: Symbolic vs Empirical Bracketing
techniques.purpose: Use symbolic systems without pretending they carry the same evidence type as psychometrics.
techniques.summary: Distinguish descriptive usefulness, symbolic resonance, and empirical status so that heterogeneous frameworks can coexist in one map.
steps: State the framework's epistemic basis.
State its social or symbolic usefulness separately.
Preserve both without collapsing either into the other.
cautions: Inclusion in the map does not imply equal evidence.

techniques.name: Result Atom Decomposition
techniques.purpose: Break whole-test outputs into smaller reasoning units that can be recombined across systems.
techniques.summary: Normalize a result into source framework, construct, output type, value, confidence, and mapped motifs so agents can reason across parts rather than only whole labels.
steps: Extract construct-level outputs.
Attach evidence and confidence.
Map to house motifs without deleting source provenance.
cautions: Do not infer person-level truth from one atom in isolation.

protocols.name: Paradox Finder
protocols.purpose: Surface load-bearing contradictions, layer mismatches, and unresolved tensions across frameworks, constructs, motifs, or result atoms without averaging them away.
protocols.summary: A compact index program that packages paradox scanning and contradiction preservation into a reusable analysis pass. It can stand alone or serve as a component program inside larger synthesis workflows.
required_inputs: result atoms or comparable comparative signals
protocols.notes: Useful both as a standalone analysis program and as a reusable component inside larger synthesis programs such as ILENS or Human Model Card.

protocols.name: ILENS
protocols.purpose: Integrate multiple personality, symbolic, behavioral, and relational systems into a layered synthesis useful for learning, emotional navigation, and adaptive interaction.
protocols.summary: ILENS is a downstream synthesis program that treats frameworks as partial languages of personhood, preserves contradiction, and derives higher-order working parameters without collapsing everything into one test.
protocols.notes: ILENS is no longer treated as the ontology itself. It is an opinionated consumer of the registry, house synthesis layer, and index-program layer.

protocols.name: Human Model Card
protocols.purpose: Produce a formal, evidence-stratified report that models a person as an evolving cognitive-behavioral system rather than as a flattering type label.
protocols.summary: A report program that uses model-card language to organize personhood evidence, contradictions, deployment conditions, and failure modes.
required_inputs: behavioral corpus or comparable evidence bundle
registry records for any referenced frameworks
protocols.notes: This index program belongs to the applied synthesis layer. It should not be mistaken for canonical framework data.

protocols.name: Translation Memo
protocols.purpose: Generate an evidence-aware memo about overlap, divergence, and incommensurability between selected frameworks or constructs.
protocols.summary: A compact comparative program for agents that need to explain how two or more systems connect without forcing a single unified language.
protocols.notes: Translation memos are useful baseline artifacts for both curation and downstream synthesis.

protocols.name: Contextual Comparison Memo
protocols.purpose: Compare one subject across time slices, roles, or contexts without confusing sparse deltas, adaptive overlays, and genuine baseline change.
protocols.summary: A comparison program for repeated or context-tagged personhood evidence that keeps stable-versus-adaptive framing, paradox preservation, and missingness explicit rather than smoothing them into one narrative arc.
required_inputs: context-tagged result atoms or comparable structured outputs
consistent comparative axes or motif traces
protocols.notes: Best used when the same or comparable frameworks have been collected for more than one context, role, or time slice. Sparse coverage should reduce the density and confidence of the output rather than forcing a narrative.

protocols.name: Pairwise Relational Comparison
protocols.purpose: Compare two subject stacks side by side without collapsing convergence, friction, orthogonality, and missingness into one compatibility score.
protocols.summary: A comparison program for pairwise or relationship-adjacent work that uses translation, paradox preservation, and evidence bracketing to keep relational claims scoped to what the inputs can actually support.
required_inputs: two explicitly separated stacks or structured result bundles
framework records for any compared systems
declared comparison question or relationship context
protocols.notes: This program is for disciplined pairwise comparison, not deterministic compatibility scoring. It should preserve asymmetry and leave unsupported seams visible.

protocol_packs.title: ILENS Core Trait-Motive Stack
protocol_packs.summary: A baseline ILENS bundle spanning Big Five, MBTI, and Enneagram to support multi-layer synthesis across trait scaffold, cognitive-style language, and motive or identity patterning.
protocol_packs.notes: This is the strongest general-purpose starting pack for downstream synthesis because it covers stable trait, style language, and identity or motive-heavy framing in one bundle.

protocol_packs.title: Attachment and Care Translation Pack
protocol_packs.summary: A translation pack for relating attachment-style outputs to relational care signaling through Love Languages without claiming one-to-one equivalence.
protocol_packs.notes: This pack is useful for relational translation and for checking where care-signaling language and attachment regulation get conflated.

protocol_packs.title: Symbolic Stack Translation Pack
protocol_packs.summary: A translation pack for Human Design and natal astrology that foregrounds symbolic meaning load, identity adhesion, and non-equivalence rather than empirical flattening.
protocol_packs.notes: This pack is especially useful for symbolic systems that are culturally sticky and interpretively thick but not psychometric in the usual sense.

protocol_packs.title: Human Model Card Personality Baseline
protocol_packs.summary: A baseline pack for Human Model Card workflows when the available person evidence includes Big Five, MBTI, and Enneagram material as structured inputs rather than raw narrative alone.
protocol_packs.notes: This pack does not replace the need for broader behavioral corpus evidence, but it gives downstream agents a consistent baseline bundle for model-card synthesis work.

protocol_packs.title: Contextual Core Trait-Motive Stack
protocol_packs.summary: A contextual comparison pack for repeated Big Five, MBTI, and Enneagram slices across time, role, or self-state while keeping stable-versus- adaptive interpretation explicit.
protocol_packs.notes: Use when the same comparative axes appear across more than one slice of a single subject. This pack is not a general pairwise or compatibility pack.

protocol_packs.title: Pairwise Relational Baseline
protocol_packs.summary: A pairwise comparison pack that centers attachment, relational care signaling, and broad trait scaffold without collapsing them into one score.
protocol_packs.notes: This is a disciplined baseline for pairwise or relationship-oriented work. It emphasizes regulation, care signaling, and broad trait context while keeping unsupported relational claims visible.

promotion_registry.name: Research Promotion Registry
promotion_registry.summary: Staged rules for moving privacy-minimizing research contributions from raw intake toward reviewed house synthesis or protocol revision without letting anecdote overwrite canonical framework records.

stages.name: Anecdotal
stages.summary: A single contribution or small set of low-density observations that may be suggestive but is not yet fit to change house synthesis.
entry_criteria: contribution was received in a supported research model
exit_criteria: multiple related contributions can be grouped or reviewed

stages.name: Normalized Input
stages.summary: A structured contribution that is transport-safe and ready for aggregation or comparative analysis.
entry_criteria: payload conforms to an approved schema such as result atoms
exit_criteria: inputs can be grouped by construct, mapping, or interaction target

stages.name: Aggregated
stages.summary: Multiple related contributions have been grouped into a comparable set without yet claiming a stable pattern.
entry_criteria: repeated contributions share a target mapping, framework seam, or motif seam
exit_criteria: a reviewer can inspect consistency, disagreement, and scope conditions

stages.name: Clustered Pattern
stages.summary: Distilled observations have been grouped into a recurring pattern rather than left as isolated anecdotes.
entry_criteria: multiple observations converge around the same pattern or caveat
exit_criteria: the pattern can be compared against existing house synthesis

stages.name: Comparative Analysis
stages.summary: Structured research inputs have been turned into an analysis artifact that can inform mappings, interactions, or future review.
entry_criteria: normalized contributions are sufficient for structured comparison
exit_criteria: analysis produces explicit candidates, tensions, or confidence shifts

stages.name: Feedback Log
stages.summary: Protocol-specific success and failure feedback has been captured in a reviewable form without yet changing the protocol surface.
entry_criteria: protocol feedback references a known protocol and a concrete issue
exit_criteria: repeated feedback can be reviewed as a revision candidate

stages.name: Reviewed
stages.summary: A curator has examined the aggregated or analyzed evidence, checked for scope limits and conflicts, and decided whether promotion is warranted.
entry_criteria: reviewer can name the exact target and expected change
exit_criteria: outcome is either promoted, contested, or sent back for more evidence

stages.name: Promoted To House Mapping
stages.summary: Reviewed research has justified a mapping revision, confidence change, or a new mapping candidate in the house synthesis layer.
entry_criteria: reviewed evidence supports a change to construct or instrument mapping
exit_criteria: mapping change is encoded in the canonical house synthesis files

stages.name: Promoted To Interaction Hypothesis
stages.summary: Reviewed research has justified a new or revised interaction hypothesis.
entry_criteria: reviewed evidence supports a stable interaction claim
exit_criteria: interaction hypothesis is encoded in the interaction registry

stages.name: Promoted To House Inference
stages.summary: Reviewed research has justified a broader house inference or caution that is not limited to one mapping object.
entry_criteria: reviewed evidence supports a synthesis-level note or caveat
exit_criteria: house inference is encoded with clear provenance and scope

stages.name: Protocol Revision
stages.summary: Reviewed feedback has justified a change to a downstream protocol or technique bundle.
entry_criteria: reviewed protocol feedback identifies a recurrent failure or missing step
exit_criteria: protocol or technique update is encoded in the protocol layer

promotion_pathways.summary: Mapping votes should accumulate around a specific mapping ID before a reviewer considers changing mapping confidence, rationale, or structure.
evidence_requirements: preserve both support and rejection rates
inspect whether disagreement is global or context-specific
reviewer_questions: Is the mapping broadly supported, broadly rejected, or split by context?
Does the evidence justify a confidence shift, a rationale rewrite, or a mapping split?

promotion_pathways.summary: Pairwise relation judgments should accumulate into a reviewed candidate interaction hypothesis before changing the interaction registry.
evidence_requirements: normalize repeated relation labels for the same atom pairing
note when the relation appears context-dependent
reviewer_questions: Is the relation stable enough to formalize as an interaction hypothesis?
Should the result be marked reinforcing, tension-producing, or context-dependent?

promotion_pathways.summary: Result atom bundles should first become comparative analysis artifacts rather than direct house synthesis changes.
evidence_requirements: group atoms by seam, motif, or compare target before synthesis
avoid direct promotion from raw result bundles
reviewer_questions: What seams or tensions recur across the grouped atoms?
Which mappings or interactions need targeted review next?

promotion_pathways.summary: Distilled observations should cluster into a recurring pattern and be reviewed before they become broader house inferences or caveats.
evidence_requirements: cluster observations by linked entities or repeated caveat
keep scope and context window explicit
reviewer_questions: Is this a recurring pattern or an attractive anecdote?
Should the output be encoded as an inference, caveat, or no change?

promotion_pathways.summary: Protocol feedback should accumulate in a reviewable log before changing protocol instructions, output contracts, or technique bundles.
evidence_requirements: group feedback by protocol_id and failure mode
distinguish missing-input problems from protocol-design problems
preserve both success and failure notes
reviewer_questions: Is the protocol failing because of design, missing inputs, or misuse?
Does the fix belong in the protocol spec, a technique, or downstream guidance?

promotion_registry.notes: Promotion pathways are governance objects. They define how evidence can influence house synthesis or protocols without confusing intake data with canonical truth.

contribution_models.name: Mapping Vote
contribution_models.purpose: Collect lightweight feedback on whether a proposed mapping fits lived experience.
contribution_models.privacy_posture: No raw narrative required; contribution should stay at the judgment layer by default.
contribution_models.notes: Best default research input when the goal is to refine construct-to-motif mappings without collecting sensitive life detail.

contribution_models.name: Pairwise Relation Judgment
contribution_models.purpose: Capture whether two result atoms feel reinforcing, contradictory, orthogonal, or context-dependent.
contribution_models.privacy_posture: Structured labels first; free text only if strictly necessary.
contribution_models.notes: Useful for discovering stable tension and reinforcement patterns across systems.

contribution_models.name: Result Atom Bundle
contribution_models.purpose: Accept normalized assessment outputs without requiring the user's full raw narrative.
contribution_models.privacy_posture: Prefer normalized, minimally identifying records over raw chats, diaries, or uploads.
contribution_models.notes: Designed for agent-to-agent exchange where GNOMY or another runtime needs a compact, protocol-safe representation of user results.

contribution_models.name: Distilled Observation
contribution_models.purpose: Record short anonymized insights about how mappings, tensions, or combinations behave in practice.
contribution_models.privacy_posture: Distilled and anonymized by default; no raw transcripts in the canonical stream.
contribution_models.notes: Useful for preserving real-world synthesis insight without over-collecting sensitive detail.

contribution_models.name: Protocol Feedback
contribution_models.purpose: Capture whether a downstream protocol produced useful, misleading, or incomplete synthesis.
contribution_models.privacy_posture: Evaluate the protocol output rather than the person's raw life material.
contribution_models.notes: Keeps downstream promptcraft and runtime behavior connected back to the repository without polluting canonical framework records.

result_atom_schema.name: Result Atom Schema
result_atom_schema.purpose: Define the normalized unit a downstream runtime can send or reason over when it wants to work at the part-of-a-framework level instead of only whole-test labels.
result_atom_schema.summary: A result atom is a compact unit of assessment output with source provenance, construct identity, output value, confidence, and optional motif trace data.

required_fields.name: framework_id
required_fields.description: Canonical framework or instrument ID in this registry.

required_fields.name: construct_id
required_fields.description: Canonical construct ID when the source framework exposes construct-level output.

required_fields.name: output_type
required_fields.description: Type of output emitted by the source framework for this atom.

required_fields.name: output_value
required_fields.description: The value, label, or normalized score emitted for this atom.

optional_fields.name: confidence
optional_fields.description: Confidence the runtime assigns to this atom after normalization.

optional_fields.name: source_quality
optional_fields.description: Assessment-quality note such as official, self-reported, estimated, or inferred.

optional_fields.name: timestamp
optional_fields.description: When the atom was measured, entered, or inferred.

optional_fields.name: mapped_motif_ids
optional_fields.description: House motif IDs linked by the current registry mapping layer.

optional_fields.name: notes
optional_fields.description: Minimal local note about ambiguity, context, or transformation.
examples: user-supplied label translated into house scale

normalization_rules: Keep source framework provenance even after motif mapping.
Prefer construct-level atoms over whole-type labels when possible.
Do not invent construct IDs that do not exist in the registry.
Preserve ambiguity rather than forcing a false clean translation.
Record source quality when the atom was inferred rather than directly assessed.
caveats: Result atoms are for downstream synthesis and research, not canonical framework truth.
One atom should not be treated as a complete person-model.
Symbolic and psychometric atoms may coexist but should not be collapsed into one evidence bucket.
result_atom_schema.notes: Downstream runtimes such as GNOMY should use this schema as a transport and reasoning contract when performing part-level synthesis.
